'''Jonathan Bennett''' is a British mathematician and Professor of Mathematical Analysis at the [[University of Birmingham]]. He was a recipient of the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 2011 for "his foundational work on multilinear inequalities in [[harmonic analysis|harmonic]] and [[geometric analysis]], and for a number of major results in the theory of [[oscillatory integral]]s."<ref>{{cite web|title=London Mathematical Society Prizes 2011|url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/About_Us/news/PR0511_LMSPrizes.pdf|publisher=London Mathematical Society|accessdate=14 July 2014}}</ref>

==Education==
In 1995 he graduated with a BA in mathematics from [[Hertford College, Oxford|Hertford College]] at the [[University of Oxford]]. He went on to study for a PhD in [[harmonic analysis]] under Anthony Carbery at the [[University of Edinburgh]], graduating in 1999.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Carbery's page at Edinburgh |url=https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/school-of-mathematics/people?person=61 |website=University of Edinburgh |accessdate=7 July 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
Bennett has done postdoctoral work at the University of Edinburgh, the [[Universidad Autonoma de Madrid]] and [[Trinity College Dublin]]. He joined the University of Birmingham in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Jonathan Bennett|url=http://www.birmingham.ac.uk/schools/mathematics/people/navigation.aspx?ReferenceId=9856&Name=professor-jonathan-bennett|publisher=University of Birmingham|accessdate=14 August 2014}}.</ref> Bennett is an editor for the journals ''[[Mathematika]]'' and ''[[Quarterly Journal of Mathematics]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Quarterly Journal of Mathematics—Editorial Board |url=https://academic.oup.com/qjmath/pages/Editorial_Board |accessdate=2 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematika—Editorial Board |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematika/information/editorial-board |accessdate=2 July 2019}}</ref>

Bennett is known for his work in harmonic analysis, particularly in applying the methods of heat flow monotonicity and induction-on-scale arguments to prove inequalities arising in harmonic and geometric analysis,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bennett |first1=Jonathan |title=Harmonic Analysis and Partial Differential Equations |date=2010 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=978-0-8218-4770-1 |pages=85–96 |chapter=Heat-flow monotonicity related to some inequalities in Euclidean analysis}}</ref> in particular for his work (jointly with Anthony Carbery and [[Terence Tao]]) on the [[Kakeya set| multilinear Kakeya conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bennett |first1=Jonathan |last2=Carbery |first2=Anthony |last3=Tao |first3=Terence |title=On the multilinear restriction and Kakeya conjectures |journal=Acta Math. |date=2006 |volume=196 |issue=2 |pages=261–302 |doi=10.1007/s11511-006-0006-4 |doi-access=free |arxiv=math/0509262 }}</ref> Bennett has an Erdős number of 3, via his collaboration with Tao.
